business_problem: Copado's growing multi-cloud environment generated thousands of security alerts a day from siloed tools. The security team needed to correlate code, cloud, and infrastructure context, prioritize important vulnerabilities, and maintain FedRAMP commitments without slowing software delivery.
solution_summary: Copado implemented Armis from ServiceNow as an AI-powered asset-intelligence and orchestration layer across its application estate. The platform correlates asset, code, cloud, and container context across AWS and Google Cloud GovCloud, then filters false positives such as internal or deprecated tools so engineering teams can focus on verified, high-impact risks. Copado rolled the deployment out across five core groups and assigned Security Champions to own risks within engineering squads. Armis reports high-fidelity findings and supports automated, risk-based prioritization; Copado also embeds security policies into its CI/CD pipeline so infrastructure-as-code misconfigurations and exposed credentials can be blocked before production. Reports are shared with Security Champions to support remediation and SLA governance. The source does not identify a model or underlying data-store product.

data_flow: Asset and vulnerability information from Copado's AWS, Google Cloud GovCloud, code, and container estate is contextualized in Armis; prioritized findings are shared with Security Champions and security policies are enforced in the CI/CD pipeline.
business_outcome: Copado reduced alert noise by up to 70%, reported 17,000 findings remediated in a 30-day window, and reduced average remediation time to seven days while consolidating five point products.
